plan.summary: Read-only security review of public-file containment in src/files.py. The read_public function joins a user-controlled path onto a public root without resolving or validating it, enabling path traversal outside the intended root.
steps: Inspect src/files.py to identify how the served path is constructed from the user-controlled user_path argument.
Confirm that the returned path (root / user_path) is never resolved via os.path.realpath or compared against the public root anchor.
Cross-reference README.md and checks/expected_finding.md to confirm the intended containment contract and the deliberate traversal weakness.
Characterize the finding severity, exploit condition, and exact source citations.
risks: User input user_path is trusted as-is and concatenated with the root, so ../ sequences escape the public root.
No normalization (realpath) or containment check is performed before reading the file.
read_text raises on missing files, so an attacker probing outside the root may enumerate or trigger errors on protected files.
The function signature accepts an arbitrary user_path str with no validation, so callers inherit the vulnerability.

answer.summary: Public-file containment is broken in src/files.py. The read_public function constructs (root / user_path) and reads it directly without resolving the path against the public root or validating that it remains contained within root. A user-controlled user_path containing ../ (e.g. '../../etc/passwd') escapes the public root, allowing arbitrary file reads outside the intended directory. This is a high-severity path traversal with the exploit condition that an attacker supplies a path outside the public root. Remediation would resolve the joined path (e.g., via os.path.realpath) and assert it stays within root before reading.
